pixel_convention: x right, y down, pixel (i,j) centre at integer coords; positions are sub-pixel circle fits to the object silhouette (threshold max(RGB) > 18 on near-black space background)

camera.motion: static (planet centre constant to +-0.05 px over all 100 frames; no background features move)
camera.perspective_cues: none (black space background, no ground plane or horizon). Only cue: moon apparent diameter shrinks ~27.9 -> ~26.6 px (about -4.8 %) over the clip, so the moon is moving slightly away from the camera; planet apparent size is constant.
camera.focal_length: unknown; estimate per question from depth_info + known size (sphere: diameter_px ~ f * D / depth)

objects.name: planet
objects.description: large banded Jupiter-like gas giant (cream/brown bands, red spot lower left), centre of image, pole tilted towards camera
objects.note: origin fixed; surface texture rotates slowly in place (spin), centre does not move

objects.name: moon
objects.description: small grey-brown cratered sphere (Io/Callisto-like moon), below-right of planet
objects.occluded: never (never overlaps planet or frame edge)
objects.motion_summary_px: moves right and up along a gently curving (concave-up in image, turning upward) arc, consistent with part of an orbit around the planet seen obliquely; per-frame pixel step decreases smoothly from ~4.2 px (start) to ~3.1 px (end); heading turns from -8 deg to -27 deg (image coords, negative = upward); image distance to planet centre grows 431.7 -> 605.2 px

events.event: moon in motion for the whole clip (no start/stop, bounce or contact)
no contact / occlusion between moon and planet
